CHEMISTRY — MOCK EXAM #9
====

GRADE: Grade 11
SUBJECT: CHEMISTRY
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which change is a physical change? (1 mark)
   A. Paper burning to ash
   B. Milk souring
   C. Ice melting to water
   D. Iron rusting

2. Photosynthesis mainly produces: (1 mark)
   A. Only water vapour
   B. Glucose and oxygen
   C. Nitrogen gas only
   D. Only carbon dioxide

3. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. Heating until a solid melts
   B. Movement of water only across a membrane
   C. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration
   D. A chemical reaction forming ash

4. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. A compound can be separated by filtering only
   B. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A mixture always has a fixed melting point

5. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Water removes heat too quickly
   B. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely
   C. Water always increases oxygen
   D. Petrol fires have no fuel

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying The Mole? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to The Mole.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about The Mole.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for The Mole.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on The Mole.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons Page 11 of 30 1 STRAND 1.0: INORGANIC CHEMISTRY.

8. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. Any white crystal used in cooking
   C. A mixture of two liquids
   D. Any substance that conducts electricity

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Reaction Rates ● Collision theory and activation energy. ● Physical changes that.

10. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 100 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 37 °C

11. The SI unit of force is the: (1 mark)
   A. watt (W)
   B. pascal (Pa)
   C. joule (J)
   D. newton (N)

12. Soil erosion is reduced by: (1 mark)
   A. Planting cover crops and terracing slopes
   B. Overgrazing continuously
   C. Burning crop residue every week
   D. Removing all vegetation

13. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Hydrocarbons ● Occurrence of organic compounds. ● Fractional distillation of cru.

14. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Gas Laws ● Boyle’s and Charles’ law. ● Combined gas law equation. ● Graham’s law.

15. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts ● Action of heat on salts (carbonates and hydrogen carbonates, nitrates, a.

   A. Producers
   B. Primary consumers only
   C. Tertiary consumers
   D. Decomposers only

   D. Guess results without recording observations on The mole 1.2. Non-metals 2.0 Physical Chemistry 2.1. Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Rea.

19. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   C. Skip labelling diagrams related to Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Salts 2.2. Gas Laws 2.3 Reaction Rates 3.0 Organic Chemistry 3.1 Hydrocarbons Pa.

----
